previous_findings.finding: Baseline classification is calculated for a scope but stored only on globally shared nodes. When a node first indexed as an addition in scope A appears in the initial scan of scope B, its existing baseline=false survives conflict handling and is returned for B. Conversely a node originally baseline in another scope can never be classified as an addition in an already-baselined new scope. This contradicts scope-specific baseline/addition semantics.
previous_findings.repair: Persist baseline/newly-indexed classification per scope membership while retaining global physical node identity and firstSeen as intended. Add same-node/two-scopes tests for both directions.

previous_findings.finding: Ingest overwrites instrument payload contentPaths with the latest partial adapter output. Although physical_members retains earlier rows, read() never queries it and no member generation/stale state is recorded. A SINE instrument with Close+Room followed by a partial Close-only scan loses Room from the reconstructed catalog and its absence cannot be distinguished from complete membership.
previous_findings.repair: Retain/reconstruct all known physical memberships with per-member observation/stale state, or expose an equivalent honest historical membership projection. Do not silently claim old members are current. Add a partial mic-loss/reopen fixture with an unchanged representative anchor.

resolved: P1 Baseline classification is stored/read on scope_members, preserving each scope independently of shared physical node identity.

P2 Physical membership generations are persisted and reconstructed into contentPaths and contentMembers with stale flags; partial mic loss retains previous membership without presenting it as currently observed.
